assessments.rationale: Active, public SDG implementation and financing coordination are documented in July 2026. The evidence supports a convergence watch, but not a secret command grid or automatic loss of national legal authority.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise only on enforceable cross-domain mandates, identity/payment linkage, sanctions or loss of domestic opt-out.

assessments.rationale: BIS Project Agorá has demonstrated tokenised multi-currency wholesale settlement and is moving toward real-value tests. The ECB digital euro pilot is also advancing. This supports common payment-rail convergence, not a single world currency.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise only if currencies are legally merged, national alternatives removed or a universal retail settlement unit becomes mandatory.

assessments.rationale: International policy harmonisation is active through the SDGs, HLPF, health, finance and technical standards. These mechanisms shape domestic policy, but current evidence does not show a sovereign global government with direct universal coercive power.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise on binding supranational enforcement that bypasses domestic ratification, courts or meaningful withdrawal.

assessments.rationale: European digital-identity wallets, high-assurance onboarding and age-verification integration are in active 2026 rollout. The permission-layer risk is materially advanced, although official policy retains voluntary use and selective-disclosure safeguards.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise if major services become practically inaccessible without wallet use or if payments, speech, health, travel and benefits are linked to one credential.

assessments.rationale: Digital currencies, identity wallets and compliance systems are advancing, but the reviewed official records do not establish a fused Western CBDC–digital-ID–social-credit enforcement system.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise only on records showing identity-linked payment restrictions based on behavioural or political compliance.

assessments.rationale: Climate, water and smart-city programmes are active, but the July 2026 sweep did not identify a general law imposing climate lockdowns, universal personal carbon allowances or neighbourhood confinement.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise on enacted individual mobility rationing, personal carbon quotas or enforceable access restrictions tied to identity.

assessments.rationale: War and security crises continue to expand defence spending, data sharing, procurement and resilience systems. The historical and current mechanism is credible, but each alleged permanent power transfer still requires a named law or contract.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise on emergency measures becoming ordinary law, permanent contractor authority, or censorship/surveillance retained after the crisis.

assessments.rationale: WHO's GDHCN is an operational global trust infrastructure built from pandemic certificate systems and is expanding toward additional health-document use cases. It does not currently give WHO personal data or prove a universal mandatory health pass.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise if access to travel, work, benefits or public life becomes broadly conditional on a persistent health credential.

assessments.rationale: Water, agriculture, fertiliser and resilience policy increasingly combines regulation, public-private finance, digital monitoring and supply coordination. This is real governance convergence, but not proof of a single actor controlling food, land and water.
assessments.falsificationStandard: Raise on ownership concentration, mandatory data/credential linkage, exclusion of small producers or loss of lawful local alternatives.
